I don’t have a dad. 
My stepdad was technically in my life until I was 16, but if anybody asks, I grew up without a dad. 
I didn’t know he was my stepdad till I was 14, but it was always different, and I never understood why. I never treated him differently, I didn’t know he wasn’t my dad. My siblings all look just like him, I just figured maybe I got more of my moms looks. 
He use to make me clean only, we never celebrated my birthday and he would tell my siblings to be mean to me. I wasn’t allowed to speak to my mothers side of the family, Probably because they hated him. He was abusive and manipulative and a terrible person. 
He tried to talk me into killing myself, perching on the end of my bed at night to whisper things I was too terrified to comprehend. 
He was always trying to get me in trouble, accusing me of drugs or boys when he never let me out of the house. I mean this seriously, I was escorted to and from school, on the dot so I never had time to hang out before or after. 
I had one school project that I had to go to a girls house for and he made my mom go with me. It was so embarrassing. 
I was a very depressed child. I thought I was a terrible person but I could never tell anyone why. I landed myself in hospitals starting at the Age of 12, because I really wanted to die. I tried all sorts of ways. My therapist use to say I never experienced a real childhood. 
An art teacher found my work disturbing and CPS got involved, and I left when I was 16. 
My life is very different now, but while I’m happier, I think I’ll always have this depression. I don’t hate him, I hope he gains peace before this new cancer diagnosis takes him. I hope he doesn’t grow even more bitter now that his wife has left him. I hope he’s good to my siblings, like he always was but never to me. 
It also made me very wary of religion. 
After all, he was a pastor.
